title: Clean only as much as you need

blocks.text: The page says streams are lazy: intermediate operations run only when a terminal operation pulls elements, and operations such as `findFirst()` and `anyMatch()` are short-circuiting. Its pitfall is collecting a whole filtered list just to look at its first element, which processes the entire stream.

Write `FirstMatch.first(List<String> raw, Function<String, String> clean, Predicate<String> wanted)`. It applies `clean` to the elements of `raw`, in order, and returns the first cleaned value that `wanted` accepts, or an empty `Optional` if none does.

items: `clean` may be expensive: call it only on the elements up to and including the first match, never on the rest.
`raw` may contain `null` elements: skip them without calling `clean` on them.

cases.says: The first cleaned value the predicate accepts comes back, in list order.
When no value matches, the answer is an empty Optional, not an exception.
The cleaning function runs only on the elements up to the first match.
A null element is skipped and never handed to the cleaning function.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: Behaviour is passed as lambdas or method references to built-in functional interfaces such as Function and Predicate.
Intermediate operations are lazy and run only as far as the terminal operation pulls elements.
findFirst and anyMatch short-circuit, so collecting a whole list to test its first element wastes work.
